summary.text: Male infant vaccinated with BCG on November 29, 2022 who developed sudden bouts of high fever (38°C) on March 29, 2023, with decreased humoral immunity and zero T and NK cell counts on April 4, 2023. Genetic analysis on April 11, 2023 revealed JAK3-associated SCID (two JAK3 missense variants) and NGS on April 12, 2023 showed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex group infection.

He was treated with anti-tuberculosis drugs (rifampicin, isoniazid, linezolid, with linezolid changed to oral after five days), received HSCT on July 11, 2023, and had isoniazid and linezolid long term. The injection-site abscess burst in April 2023 and sore cleaning with suture surgery was done on June 21, 2023. He recovered well. The causal association with BCG vaccination was inconclusive but could not be disregarded.

summary.text: Female infant vaccinated with BCG on September 3, 2022 and with an oral pentavalent rotavirus vaccine on October 28, 2022. Rashes appeared on her back and hands on October 29, 2022, then spread with fever, cough and lymphadenopathy. Genetic analysis on November 2, 2022 revealed TNFRSF13B-associated SCID; blood tests on November 29, 2022 showed decreased IgA, IgG and IgM, and NGS on January 10, 2023 detected bovine-type Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex infection in blood, marrow and alveolar lavage fluid.

She was treated with rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol, linezolid and levofloxacin, received HSCT on May 25, 2023, and died on October 2, 2023 after repeated mixed infections of multiple pathogens, septic shock, pulmonary hemorrhage, acute respiratory distress syndrome and multi-organ failure on the basis of SCID. The causal association between disseminated BCG infection and BCG vaccination was confirmed.

summary.text: Male infant vaccinated with BCG on June 2, 2024 who had sudden hypersomnia and ashen complexion on June 8, 2024 and a fever of 37.4℃ on July 1, 2024. Lymphocyte testing on July 4, 2024 showed decreased CD4/CD8 double-positive and several B lymphocyte subsets and increased total, helper and primary helper T lymphocytes; NGS on July 8, 2024 showed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex group infection, and genetic testing on July 16, 2024 found missense mutations in CR2, IFNAR2 and TLR2 and a suspected DOCK11 exon 13 duplication.

He was treated with rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and linezolid (linezolid changed to oral one week later), recovered well two weeks later, and received rifampicin, isoniazid and linezolid long term. The causal association with BCG vaccination was inconclusive but could not be disregarded.

article_limitations: The article has no figures or supplements; no visual review applies.
Table 1 has no time scope; table-sourced facts (age of onset, outcomes, treatment classes) carry no time.
Several sentences state events without a date (treatment regimens, recovery); no order is inferred from paragraph order. Case 3 'Two weeks later' has no named reference point.
The causal-association statement names case 2 as confirmed and 'the other two cases' as inconclusive; cases 1 and 3 are inferred only by that exclusion.
Discussion statements about the three cases in aggregate (JAK3, TNF and TLR2 defects; only one had an injection-site abscess) are not assigned to individuals.
Case 1 text mentions HSCT on July 11, 2023 before giving the drug regimen; the drug start dates are not stated.
